Yes. Blog flow needs two gates:

`write → inspect → publish`

| StageWhat happens |                                                                             |
| ----------------- | --------------------------------------------------------------------------- |
| Draft             | Write one MDX file on `blog/<slug>` branch.                                 |
| PR preview        | Vercel creates rendered URL.                                                |
| Stable preview    | Merge to `main`; `preview.dhruv2mars.com` updates.                          |
| Visual QA         | Check desktop/mobile, light/dark, typography, links, code, images, OG card. |
| Publish           | Change frontmatter `status: draft` → `published`. Preview again.            |
| GA                | You approve exact deployment. Promote immutable build to production.        |
| Rollback          | Re-point production to previous approved deployment.                        |

Draft posts should:

- show `DRAFT` banner on preview;
- remain accessible by direct slug on preview;
- stay out of blog index, search, RSS, sitemap, and JSON-LD;
- never appear on production accidentally.

Frontmatter:
```yaml
title: ...
description: ...
status: draft
publishedAt: 2026-08-21
tags: [...]
```

Automated checks:

- MDX/frontmatter schema
- duplicate slugs
- broken internal links
- missing images
- lint, typecheck, tests
- production build
- OG metadata
- RSS/sitemap output

Your job: write content. System job: render it, test it, expose preview, block unsafe release.

Recommended additions:
```arduino
bun run blog:new "Post title"
bun run blog:check
```

No CMS needed yet. MDX stays source of truth. Main branch becomes preview. Production only changes through explicit approval.

content.text:
Strong plan. I’d adopt it.

Core flow right:

`MDX → PR preview → stable main preview → visual QA → explicit immutable promotion`

Main gaps:

- Frontmatter mismatch. Plan says `status` + `description`; repo currently uses `draft` + `summary`. Pick one canonical schema. Recommend:

```yaml
title: ...
description: ...
status: draft
publishedAt: 2026-08-21
tags:
  - ...
```

- Draft visibility needs two separate rules:
  - Preview: direct slug works, `DRAFT` banner, `noindex`.
  - Production: direct slug returns 404.
  - Every index, search, home, nav, RSS, sitemap, and JSON-LD path excludes drafts.

  Current [lib/blog.ts](/Users/dhruv2mars/dev/github/portfolio/lib/blog.ts) hides drafts from detail routes too, so this needs an environment-aware split.

- `blog:check` must be a real release gate, not convenience tooling. Add checks for schema, duplicate slugs, dates, internal links, image files, MDX compile, OG output, RSS, sitemap, production draft leakage.

- Promotion must target exact reviewed deployment ID/SHA. Never promote “latest main.” Record approved deployment for rollback.

- `blog/<slug>` branch naming works. Branch names are not security. Protected `release` branch + Vercel Production Branch are the real guard.

- Add explicit tests for:
  - Draft slug works on preview.
  - Draft slug 404s in production.
  - Draft emits no JSON-LD.
  - Draft emits `noindex`.
  - Draft never enters RSS/sitemap/search/index.
  - Published post passes all output checks.

Repo already has most release shape in [0006-preview-first-release-lane.md](/Users/dhruv2mars/dev/github/portfolio/docs/adr/0006-preview-first-release-lane.md) and [docs/release-process.md](/Users/dhruv2mars/dev/github/portfolio/docs/release-process.md). Missing pieces: `blog:new`, `blog:check`, `status` schema, preview-only draft routes, DRAFT banner, CI enforcement.

Verdict: good workflow. Add those invariants, then it becomes safe.
